North Korean Hackers Moved $38M Through Relay Protocol in 7 Hours On-chain analyst Specter reported that North Korean hackers transferred approximately $38 million through Relay Protocol within seven hours, with transfers still ongoing at the time of the post. Despite Relay's claims of having a Know Your Transaction (KYT) monitoring system in place, it failed to block the transfers. Specter noted that North Korean hackers would have struggled to move such a large amount through THORChain in the same timeframe, raising questions about Relay's compliance and risk controls. Relay Protocol is a cross-chain bridge and interoperability protocol that enables asset transfers across multiple blockchains. — link

Highlight Clip: Binance Co-CEO: Attackers Used Self-Destruct Mechanisms, Making the Hack Harder to Trace Binance Co-CEO: Attackers Used Self-Destruct Mechanisms, Making the Hack Harder to Trace Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng updated the investigation into the roughly $6.3 billion hack on October 30, saying multiple people were involved. Investigators initially suspected a compromised laptop but later found other entry points. Attackers used self-destruct mechanisms to erase tools and traces, complicating the investigation. Teng said they used EIP-7702 to gain on-chain execution authority over a hot wallet without passing Binance's normal approval controls. Binance paused withdrawals to rebuild and test its systems, targeting restoration within 40 hours. It is also working with law enforcement to trace and recover stolen funds. — link

Binance to Resume Withdrawals in Phases From 06:00 to 09:00 UTC Today, With 95% of Affected Assets Replenished Binance announced plans to gradually resume the first phase of withdrawals between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC on November 1, covering 15 networks including BTC, ETH, BSC, and SOL. Other networks will reopen after security checks are completed, while deposits remain operational. Binance also said it has replenished approximately 95% of affected assets, up from 90% previously. BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC are now all backed by 100% reserves. The remaining 5% consists of less liquid tokens that Binance is still acquiring. The exchange reiterated its commitment to covering all losses from the hack. — link

OneKey Founder: Some Older iPhones Have Unpatchable Chip Vulnerabilities, Posing Risks to Seed Phrase Storage OneKey founder Yishi warned that factory-resetting an older iPhone, enabling airplane mode, and using it to store crypto wallet seed phrases offline may still be unsafe. He noted that iPhone 4S through iPhone X are affected by checkm8, while iPhone XS, XR, 11 series, and second-generation iPhone SE are affected by usbliter8, disclosed earlier this year. These BootROM-level vulnerabilities cannot be fixed through iOS updates. Attackers with physical access and specialized tools may exploit them via USB, even in airplane mode. However, on models such as the XS and 11, these flaws alone do not provide direct access to seed phrases, as device passcodes and the Secure Enclave offer additional protection. Yishi advised affected users to generate entirely new seed phrases in a trusted environment, transfer their assets, use newer devices, keep software updated, and adopt stronger passwords. — link
